ai.seo_question: Who were the two arbitrators' companions described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Shia scholars interpret this passage as a critique of the political compromise at Siffin, portraying the arbitrators' followers as a heterogeneous group of 'amateurs' lacking the spiritual depth of the Muhajirun and Ansar. The description highlights their need for rigorous theological and moral training, reflecting the Shia view that their elevation was due to political expediency rather than intrinsic merit. This underscores the distinction between mere political allegiance and true religious authority in early Islamic history.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Rude, low people and mean slaves.
